subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) reported 3 affected individuals from 2 families who had a similar skeletal phenotype: a 7-year-old boy whose phenotype most closely resembled Cole-Carpenter syndrome, and 2 fetuses first suspected to have a severe type of osteogenesis imperfecta. All 3 had severely disturbed ossification of the skull and multiple fractures beginning before birth. The boy also had short stature and craniofacial malformations, including macrocephaly, midface hypoplasia, micrognathia, frontal bossing and down-slanting palpebral fissures.

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) used whole-exome sequencing to find 3 mutant SEC24D alleles in 3 affected individuals from 2 families. Each affected individual was compound heterozygous for 2 of these alleles. SEC24D encodes a component of the COPII complex, which is involved in protein export from the endoplasmic reticulum.

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.3044C>T missense mutation in SEC24D, causing a p.Ser1015Phe substitution in a cargo-binding pocket. It was found in the compound heterozygous state in all 3 affected individuals from 2 families. The variant lay within a 14-Mb founder haplotype shared by all 3 individuals.

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.613C>T truncating mutation in SEC24D, resulting in p.Gln205Ter. Patients carried it in the compound heterozygous state together with another SEC24D mutation.

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) identified a c.2933A>C missense mutation in SEC24D, causing a p.Gln978Pro substitution in the gelsolin-like domain. Patients carried it in the compound heterozygous state together with another SEC24D mutation.

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) examined skin fibroblasts from the affected boy using electron and immunofluorescence microscopy. Export of procollagen from the endoplasmic reticulum was inefficient and the ER tubules were dilated, reproducing the cellular phenotype seen in cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia caused by SEC23A mutations. The authors noted that the cellular and morphologic phenotypes matched those described in Sec24d-deficient fish mutants: vbi (medaka) and bulldog (zebrafish).

subject: Garbes et al. (2015)
object: Garbes et al. (2015) noted that cranio-lenticulo-sutural dysplasia, caused by SEC23A mutations, has a largely overlapping craniofacial phenotype. Unlike the SEC24D disorder, however, it does not feature generalized bone fragility, and the original family described had cataracts.

subject: Moosa et al. (2016)
object: Moosa et al. (2016) reported that mutations in the SEC24D gene cause autosomal recessive osteogenesis imperfecta.

subject: Zhang et al. (2017)
object: Zhang et al. (2017) described a 23-year-old Chinese man (family 1) with recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, an open anterior fontanel, and facial dysmorphism. CT 3-dimensional imaging of the cranium showed skull deformities with a broad ossification defect in the frontoapical area, a widened sagittal suture, and wormian bones.

subject: Zhang et al. (2017)
object: Zhang et al. (2017) described a 7-year-old Chinese boy (family 2) who had recurrent fractures, dentinogenesis imperfecta, and an open anterior fontanel, but no obvious facial dysmorphism.

subject: Zhang et al. (2017)
object: Using whole-exome sequencing in the proband from family 1, Zhang et al. (2017) identified novel compound heterozygous missense mutations in the SEC24D gene: c.2723G>A (p.Cys908Tyr) and c.2842T>C (p.Ser948Pro).

subject: Zhang et al. (2017)
object: Using whole-exome sequencing in the proband from family 2, Zhang et al. (2017) identified novel compound heterozygous missense mutations in the SEC24D gene: c.938G>A (p.Arg313His) and c.875C>T (p.Pro292Leu).

subject: Takeyari et al. (2018)
object: Takeyari et al. (2018) described a 15-year-old Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome. He had short-trunk short stature and craniofacial abnormalities, including ocular proptosis, marked frontal bossing, midface hypoplasia, and micrognathia. He also had low bone mineral density and basilar impression.

subject: Takeyari et al. (2018)
object: Takeyari et al. (2018) used whole exome sequencing to identify compound heterozygous variants in the SEC24D gene, p.Arg484* and p.Arg313His, in a Japanese boy with Cole-Carpenter syndrome type 2.
